extracted.intended_audience: readers and translators of classic Hindu folk-tales; general literary readers interested in folklore, the supernatural, and Victorian translations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and descriptive criteria for translating, selecting, arranging, and presenting classical Hindu tales (Baital-Pachisi) for an English-reading public, with attention to style, framing, and audience taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit: suggestiveness and general applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: “The merit of the old stories lies in their suggestiveness and in their general applicability.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text explicitly identifies suggestiveness and broad applicability as central virtues of these tales—stories should provoke thought and apply to many situations rather than being narrowly literal. The editor/translator expands terse originals to make these virtues perceptible to readers (see guidance on clothing the skeleton with flesh and blood).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tales should insinuate a moral or lesson by amusing narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: These tales, 'by amusing narrative and romantic adventure, insinuates a lesson in morals or in humanity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective stories entertain via narrative and adventure while embedding ethical or humane lessons subtly; readers may not always perceive the didactic drift, so the storytelling should balance amusement with clarity of underlying lesson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translator's linguistic intimacy improves value
rubrics_metrics.description: “This translation is rendered peculiarly valuable and interesting by Sir Richard Burton’s intimate knowledge of the language.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A translator's deep understanding of the source language and culture is a key quality metric: it produces a translation that preserves wit, registers, idioms, and cultural nuance, making the work lively and authentic for the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and abridge for reader interest
rubrics_metrics.description: “My husband only gives eleven of the best tales, as it was thought the translation would prove more interesting in its abbreviated form.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curating a subset of 'best' tales (abridgement) is an accepted editorial choice to maintain reader engagement; selection should favor stories that exemplify genre strengths and suit intended readership and format length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a framing device to string tales together
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection is described as 'a string of fine pearls to be hung round the neck of human intelligence' and the narrative 'turns chiefly on a great king named Vikram' (i.e., the frame story).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ a coherent frame narrative (here Vikram and the Vampire/Baital-Pachisi) to provide continuity and context for otherwise separate tales; the frame can supply stakes, repetition, and thematic unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match content to audience tastes (weird, supernatural, grotesque)
rubrics_metrics.description: “It will especially please those who delight in the weird and supernatural, the grotesque, and the wild life.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about genre tone and audience expectations; emphasize elements (supernatural, grotesque, adventurous) that appeal to the target readers and shape selection and translation choices accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative purity vs. licentiousness — restraint when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: The preface argues that 'this looseness, resulting from the separation of the sexes, is accidental, not necessary...it can be dispensed with, and that there is such a thing as comparative purity in Hindu literature.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize cultural patterns (e.g., frankness/looseness) but exercise editorial judgment about including explicit material; maintain restraint when aiming to present a purer or more decorous collection for certain audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metamorphosis/transformation as an effective motif
rubrics_metrics.description: The preface highlights stories built on metamorphosis (e.g., Lucius into an ass, Gandharba-Sena transformed) as fundamental plot engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformation motifs (metamorphosis, curses, shape-change) operate as compelling narrative devices—use them to explore identity, irony, and moral consequence; they are characteristic structural elements of these tales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include cultural detail to increase interest and authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: The tales 'contain much interesting information on Indian customs and manners.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve or elucidate cultural customs, rites, and social detail in translation/annotation to enrich reader understanding and lend authenticity; such details also serve informative and ethnographic interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy conciseness by 'clothing the skeleton with flesh and blood'
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor states: 'I have ventured to remedy the conciseness of their language, and to clothe the skeleton with flesh and blood.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When source texts are terse, translators/editors may expand and smooth language for readability and dramatic effect—add descriptive material, connective tissue, and character detail while respecting original intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ wit and 'chaff' (playful banter/humor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The translation is described as 'as witty, and as full of what is popularly called “chaff” as it is possible to be.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve or recreate humor, repartee, and lighthearted banter in translation to retain the original tone; playful asides and comic elements are a valued part of the genre's appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative convention: marry hero and heroine / provide closure
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor notes: 'The author, indeed, almost always takes the trouble to marry his hero and his heroine,' often resolving romantic threads by marriage or legal rites (e.g., 'gandharbavivaha').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide satisfying romantic resolution when such a convention is part of the source tradition—use culturally specific marriage rites or plausible substitutes to close romantic arcs and meet audience expectations of closure.
